verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center's Pad 39B
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '6:36 PM / April 1, 2026 Artemis II lifts off Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT.'; R2: '6:35 p.m. NASA’s Artemis II SLS ... lifted off from Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B in Florida at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R5: 'Artemis II launched ... at 5.35 p.m. Central Time [6:35 p.m. EDT] ... from Launch Pad 39B'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm exact date, time, location, and successful launch.

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket successfully sent the Orion capsule into orbit
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '6:46 PM / April 1, 2026 Core stage separates The core stage has successfully separated'; R2: '6:43 p.m. Main engine cutoff of the SLS ... core stage has successfully separated ... transition to upper‑stage operations'; R3: 'Artemis II heads to the moon: Four astronauts ... on their way ... after successfully conducting the translunar injection burn'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm SLS core stage separation and Orion achieving orbit post-launch.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule carried Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with CSA ... Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: All sources list exact crew names matching the claim.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day trip around the Moon
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'approximately 10-day Artemis II mission around the moon'; R2: 'approximately 10-day Artemis II mission around the Moon'; R3: '10 days in space'; R5: 'set to spend 10 days in space'
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as ~10-day mission looping around the Moon; minor variations (e.g., 9.5 days) do not contradict.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is safely in orbit
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '7:54 AM / April 2, 2026 Artemis II crew begins first day in space after exhilarating launch ... orbiting the Earth'; R2: 'The Orion spacecraft’s SAWs ... deployed ... in Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Post-launch updates confirm crew safe and in Earth orbit.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is conducting a 10-day mission
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the approximately 10-day Artemis II mission'; R2: 'the approximately 10-day Artemis II mission'; R5: 'set to spend 10 days in space'
verifications.reasoning: Ongoing mission explicitly described as 10-day in sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch had a minor, resolved issue with the launch-abort system battery
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '5:48 PM ... Battery issue will not affect launch ... higher-than-expected temperature ... believed to be an instrumentation issue'; R2: '5:57 p.m. ... sensor on the launch abort system’s attitude control motor controller battery ... believed to be an instrumentation issue and will not affect today’s launch'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe minor battery temperature issue with launch abort system, resolved as instrumentation problem.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch proceeded on schedule
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: Launch window 6:24 p.m., polled go 6:31, liftoff 6:35 after holds and issue resolutions; R2: 'T-10 minute hold ... extended ... new liftoff time will be set shortly' but launched at 6:35
verifications.reasoning: Launched within window shortly after planned time despite holds and issues; broadly on schedule but not precisely without delays.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission to the Moon in a generation
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago'; R2: 'first crewed flight under NASA’s Artemis campaign ... first crewed deep-space flight in over 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state first crewed lunar mission in 50+ years, matching 'in a generation'.

verifications.claim: Artemis II Launch Day Updates - NASA, the core stage has separated

verifications.evidence: R2: Title 'Artemis II Launch Day Updates - NASA'; '6:43 p.m. Main engine cutoff of the SLS ... core stage has successfully separated'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match to NASA updates title and core stage separation event.
